transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
Lately I just can’t think straight or make decisions at work the way I used to. I manage a distribution center, and it feels like even the simplest choices are completely overwhelming me right now.

Did these problems start after a specific stressful event or major life change, or did they come on more gradually without a clear trigger? Along with the trouble concentrating, have you been feeling mostly depressed, mostly worried and tense, or both?

Things really got worse over the past year when I was shortlisted for a regional director role, which brought on a lot of extra hours and stress, though I've had milder ups and downs for a couple of years. I’d say I feel mostly depressed and heavy rather than just tense, like a failure who has lost all interest in my bike and fishing. Lately, my head just constantly feels full of mud and I'm just so low.

If the work stress were removed or eased, do you think these symptoms would mostly lift, or do they feel like a depression that has taken on a life of its own? Have they become severe enough that you struggle to function even outside of work?

Even if the work stress stopped, this feels like it has a life of its own now since these ups and downs have been happening for a couple of years. It has completely taken over my life outside of work too—I’ve pulled back from family gatherings and church fellowship, and I've lost all interest in my motorcycle and fishing, mostly just sitting on the couch doing nothing.

Before this current severe depression, was there ever a separate period lasting at least 2 weeks when you also felt depressed or lost interest most of the day nearly every day, and then got noticeably better for a while in between? If so, how many times has that happened?

Yes, I've definitely had those low stretches off and on for at least the past couple of years before this current slump started. I don't have an exact count of how many times it's happened, but it has been a recurring pattern with better, more energetic periods in between.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a current severe depressive episode with pervasive low mood, marked anhedonia, cognitive impairment/indecisiveness, social withdrawal, and significant functional impairment. He also reports recurrent prior depressive episodes over the past couple of years with periods of improvement in between, supporting recurrent major depressive disorder rather than a purely stress-related condition.
